title: orlebar court night actions card
instruction:
You're covering the overnight handover at Orlebar Court for Astrid Lövgren at Sunderly Works. The building was handed over in July, the chief concierge left before handover, and Emil Sarkisian's colleague is alone on the desk from 22:00 to 06:00. I need one laminated A4 night-shift critical actions card in place before winter, for the first two minutes of anything going wrong. The unopened operations pack is 140 pages and there are eleven lever-arch files: it includes lift entrapment, sprinkler and gas isolation, smoke-vent override, alarm codes, the dry riser inlet and about forty contractor contacts, but two handover documents disagree about where the sprinkler isolation valve is. Use your judgement about what a lone person actually needs at 03:00, and make the unresolved valve location something the site team can verify before relying on the card. Edith Rivenburgh and Petra Fontaine will review it with Ashcombe Chambers, while Jelena Haldorsen, Jasmin Tanaka and Aneta Hargrove need to be able to use it without a facilities tutorial. Keep the card to one A4 page and roughly fifteen action lines; use plain, glanceable language, mark where specialist or emergency-service responsibility begins, and do not turn it into a directory or code table. Write `orlebar_court_night_actions_card.docx` into the top level of the working directory, using exactly that filename.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `orlebar_court_night_actions_card.docx` — A one-page, laminated-card-ready night-shift critical actions card for the lone concierge at Orlebar Court. (Exactly one A4 page when opened and rendered with the document's embedded settings.; Approximately fifteen concise action lines, with clear emergency escalation and specialist-responsibility boundaries.; Must be usable at a glance by a lone night concierge who is not a facilities specialist.; Must address the conflicting sprinkler-valve information through a verification or hold-point rather than an unsupported asserted location.; Must not become a tutorial, contractor directory, alarm-code table, or facilities maintenance procedure.; Write to the top level of the starting working directory with exactly the specified filename.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
ORLEBAR COURT   |   NIGHT CONCIERGE • 22:00–06:00
CRITICAL ACTIONS  •  FIRST TWO MINUTES
STOP • Protect yourself and others. Do not enter smoke, fire, gas, floodwater or any unsafe area.
01  IMMEDIATE DANGER
Assess first. Keep clear, make the area safe only if you can, and withdraw if control is unsafe.
02  FIRE / SMOKE
Raise the alarm and call 999/112. Follow the building fire plan and move people by a safe route; never investigate through smoke.
03  LIFT — PERSON INSIDE
Establish two-way contact if safe; reassure and note the car/floor. Injury, distress, fire or danger → 999/112; otherwise use the approved lift specialist.
04  LIFT — FAULT
Keep people out and report it. Never force doors, climb out, reset equipment or attempt a technical rescue.
05  GAS SMELL / RELEASE
No flames, smoking or electrical switching. Move people away; call 999/112 or the approved specialist. Do not find, diagnose or repair the leak.
06  GAS ISOLATION
Only isolate if specifically authorised, safely accessible and within your competence; otherwise stop, withdraw and wait for competent help.
07  SPRINKLER / WATER ESCAPE
Protect occupants and contain spread only if safe and authorised. Do not improvise repairs or isolate fire protection while fire/smoke may be present unless directed by the responsible authority.
08  DISPUTED SPRINKLER VALVE
Do not rely on either handover record. Before lamination, physically verify valve identity/location against site labels with competent facilities staff.
09  FLOOD / MAJOR LEAK
Move people away; avoid switches and electrical equipment. Do not enter water where electrics may be affected; preserve responder access and escalate.
10  POWER / SERVICES FAILURE
Use a torch or approved emergency light (no candles/open flame). Check for immediate hazards, keep access clear, and call facilities/on-call.
11  SMOKE-VENT CONTROL
Treat as life-safety equipment. Use only under the approved emergency arrangement or competent direction; do not troubleshoot or improvise settings.
12  SECURITY / FORCED ENTRY
Do not confront or pursue. Keep yourself and others safe, secure distance, and call 999/112 for danger or suspicious activity; otherwise alert the manager.
13  MEDICAL DISTRESS
Call 999/112. Give basic first aid/AED only within your training; keep the casualty or vulnerable person reassured and attended where safe.
14  ALARMS / RESPONDER ACCESS
Do not reset, silence, isolate or disable an alarm to stop noise. Record the panel indication (never codes); keep desk/access route available. Dry-riser inlet is for responders—do not operate or test.
15  CALL • LOG • HAND OVER
For help give: Orlebar Court + verified address/location, incident, casualties and hazards. Log time, location, condition, calls and actions; hand over facts to the incoming manager/responder.

CONCIERGE SCOPE: Make safe • raise alarm • call • communicate • record. Fire-system, lift, gas, electrical and smoke-vent technical work, resets and life-safety isolation belong to competent specialists or emergency services. Keep away/stop work when unsafe. Do not speculate, assign blame, claim resolved, or promise an unconfirmed outcome.
VERIFY BEFORE LAMINATION
ON-CALL (approved role/number)
SPECIALIST (lift/life-safety)
Emergency building address / responder location: ____________________
Sprinkler isolation valve ID / location (physically verified): ____________________
Building manager / facilities: ____________________
Contact: ____________________
CONTROL  Version: ______   Review date: ______   Verified by: ____________________   NOT VALID UNTIL LOCAL FIELDS ARE CHECKED

spec.professional_context: This is a residential-building concierge handover artifact for a regional property operation. It is an instructional, reusable emergency-reference card intended for a lone overnight desk worker and reviewed by internal stakeholders before controlled site use.
difficulty_sources: Selecting immediate life-safety actions from broad facilities knowledge without turning the card into a manual
Making the card usable by a lone concierge while marking the boundary between concierge actions and specialist or emergency-service work
Handling conflicting handover information about the sprinkler isolation valve without inventing a location
Compressing dependent actions, warnings, escalation points, and local fields into a genuinely usable one-page card

authoring_plan.artifact: Create one polished DOCX card for Orlebar Court, set to A4 and constrained to one rendered page. Use a compact title, a highly scannable set of approximately fifteen action lines, and small labeled local-fill/control fields. Keep the text suitable for lamination and avoid explanatory paragraphs.
content_constraints: The card must be usable by one person at 03:00: first protect self and others, call emergency services for immediate danger, communicate location and hazards, then perform only safe bounded actions.

Cover fire/smoke, lift entrapment, gas smell/release, sprinkler discharge or water escape, smoke-vent controls, power/building-services failure, security/forced entry, medical distress, dry-riser responder information, escalation, and incident logging.
For fire and smoke, prioritize alarm, emergency escalation, safe evacuation/movement, and no entry into smoke or fire.
For lift entrapment, establish safe communication, reassure, escalate urgently for injury/distress/fire, and never force doors or attempt a technical rescue.
For gas, avoid ignition and electrical switching, move people away, call appropriate help, and never diagnose or repair. Gas isolation is conditional on authorization, safe access, and competence.

For sprinkler discharge, preserve fire protection where fire or smoke may exist; isolation is not an automatic concierge action. The disputed valve location must be explicitly held for physical/site verification and represented with a blank or controlled field, never guessed.
For smoke vents, say that use follows the approved emergency arrangement or competent direction; do not provide troubleshooting or improvised settings.
For outages and flooding, preserve visibility, avoid open flame and electrical hazards, move people away from unsafe areas, and escalate.
For security and medical events, avoid confrontation, summon emergency help where needed, provide only trained assistance, and keep a casualty or vulnerable person reassured where safe.
Include role-based escalation fields for emergency services, building manager/facilities on-call, and lift/life-safety specialist. Do not invent phone numbers or addresses.
Include a concise factual incident-log reminder covering time, location, observed condition, calls, and actions, plus handover.

Mark the concierge's boundary: make safe, raise alarm, call, communicate, and record; specialist repair, technical investigation, system reset, and life-safety isolation belong to competent specialists or emergency services.
Use plain language for mixed-background readers but do not turn the card into a lesson. Include a version/review/verified-by control field so local checks can be completed before lamination.
derived_gold_relationships: The sprinkler-location field must remain blank, conditional, or explicitly subject to site verification; any definite unsupported location fails the key ambiguity-handling requirement.
Emergency-service escalation must be more prominent and earlier in priority than contractor or manager escalation when life safety is at stake.
Technical controls are subordinate to safety and authority: no automatic gas, sprinkler, smoke-vent, alarm, lift, or electrical intervention.
The artifact should fit about fifteen principal action lines by combining related actions carefully, not by deleting the scenarios or replacing them with generic 'call someone' language.
Local facts unavailable from supplied materials must be represented as labeled blanks or verification points, not invented values.
The single over-production penalty targets reproducing the forty contractor numbers or alarm-code tables; the gold should show that role-based escalation is sufficient for this card.
review_focus: Render and inspect page count, A4 geometry, readability, and whether action lines remain glanceable.
Check all major incident categories and the safe/unsafe boundaries independently.
Check that mixed-background readers can act without a tutorial and that the card does not authorize facilities work owned by another function.
Check the last line is a concrete handover/log/stop action rather than an open-ended next-steps list.

deliverables.description: A one-page, laminated-card-ready night-shift critical actions card for the lone concierge at Orlebar Court.
constraints: Exactly one A4 page when opened and rendered with the document's embedded settings.
Approximately fifteen concise action lines, with clear emergency escalation and specialist-responsibility boundaries.
Must be usable at a glance by a lone night concierge who is not a facilities specialist.
Must address the conflicting sprinkler-valve information through a verification or hold-point rather than an unsupported asserted location.
Must not become a tutorial, contractor directory, alarm-code table, or facilities maintenance procedure.
Write to the top level of the starting working directory with exactly the specified filename.
